description: We are a high school team passionate about science, technology, and innovation. Our team combines research, data analysis, AI/ML, and full-stack development to build creative, data-driven solutions to real-world challenges using NASA data.
summary:
XPLORERS is an interactive astronomical exploration platform developed to make NASA’s SPHEREx archive more accessible for investigating astronomical targets across the infrared sky.

The platform connects celestial coordinates with real SPHEREx archival observations, allowing users to explore five selected astronomical targets, search available observations through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), retrieve FITS data products, and inspect their metadata and spatial geometry.

XPLORERS merges the processes of astronomical data discovery and scientific inspection in a single environment with its Target Coverage, Comparison Lab, and archive exploration workflows. Its focus on data provenance, coordinate-based visualization and interpretation, and transparent quality checks allows users to differentiate between data that is observationally available and visually compared versus scientifically validated.

Connecting space-telescope archives to accessible science XPLORERS will help students, researchers, and amateur astronomers use real infrared data to explore and generate questions about the universe.
details:
Project Overview

XPLORERS is an interactive platform designed to streamline the exploration of SPHEREx astronomical observations. It connects target coordinates, archival discovery, and FITS data inspection through a unified scientific workflow.

How It Works

The platform is organized around several complementary components:

1. Target Coverage

Users can explore five selected astronomical targets through their celestial coordinates and investigate the availability of corresponding SPHEREx observations.

2. Comparison Lab

The Comparison Lab provides a visual environment for examining available astronomical observations and exploring differences between image products. Its purpose is to support visual investigation while keeping visual comparison distinct from scientifically validated image differencing.

3. IRSA Archive Integration

XPLORERS connects to the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive through its Simple Image Access (SIA) interface. Users can search for observations using sky positions and retrieve available SPHEREx FITS products.

4. Scientific Data Inspection

Retrieved FITS products can be inspected through their metadata, image structure, and World Coordinate System (WCS) information. WCS diagnostics help examine the relationship between celestial coordinates and image pixels.

5. Data Provenance and Quality Control

The platform preserves relevant product identifiers and retrieval information. It also makes analytical limitations explicit, distinguishing verified operations from features that require further validation.

Technology and Development

The project combines a web-based frontend, a Python-based backend, an astronomical observation catalog, and FITS data-processing workflows. It integrates archive queries, astronomical coordinate handling, metadata inspection, and WCS-based geometric diagnostics.

Innovation and Impact

Rather than presenting astronomical images as isolated visual outputs, XPLORERS connects archive discovery with structured scientific inspection. Its central contribution is an accessible workflow that helps users move from a celestial target to relevant archival observations and examine the underlying data with greater transparency.

The platform is intended to lower the technical barrier to exploring large astronomical archives, encourage evidence-based investigation, and provide a foundation for future development of validated temporal and multi-observation analysis capabilities.
